public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 178

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/178](https://www.erdosproblems.com/178)
- [ErGr79] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory: van der Waerden's theorem and related topics*. Enseign. Math. (1979), 325-344.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique (1980).
- [Be81] Beck, József, *Balancing families of integer sequences*. Combinatorica (1981), 209-216.
- [Be17] Beck, József, *A discrepancy problem: balancing infinite dimensional vectors*. Number theory—Diophantine problems, uniform distribution and applications (2017), 61-82.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos178

open Finset BigOperators

/--
Let $A_1,A_2,\ldots$ be an infinite collection of infinite sets of integers, say
$A_i=\{a_{i1}<a_{i2}<\cdots\}$. Does there exist some $f:\mathbb{N}\to\{-1,1\}$ such that
$$\max_{m, 1\leq i\leq d} \left\lvert \sum_{1\leq j\leq m} f(a_{ij})\right\rvert \ll_d 1$$
for all $d\geq 1$?

Erdős remarks 'it seems certain that the answer is affirmative'. This was solved by Beck [Be81]. Recently Beck [Be17] proved that one can replace $\ll_d 1$ with $\ll d^{4+\epsilon}$ for any $\epsilon>0$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos178.lean"]
theorem erdos_178 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ) (ha : ∀ i, StrictMono (a i)),
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℤ, (∀ n, f n = 1 ∨ f n = -1) ∧
      ∀ d : ℕ, ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ m i : ℕ, i < d →
        |∑ j ∈ range m, f (a i j)| ≤ ↑C := by
  sorry

end Erdos178

reformulations.difference: Lean uses strictly increasing natural-number sequences and per-d natural bounds with ≤. The original Erdős–Graham formulation speaks of integers and an existential bound function F(d), with a strict inequality.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The original sources expressly allow F to depend on the sequences, so the Lean bound has the correct dependence. Choosing the natural bounds C(d) gives F(d)=C(d)+1; conversely, round each real bound upward. Even interpreting the original integers as ℤ gives an equivalent qualitative claim: each increasing row has a nonnegative tail. Apply the natural-number statement simultaneously to those tails, color negative integers arbitrarily, and absorb each discarded finite prefix into its row's bound. Taking a finite maximum gives the required bound for i<d. The converse follows by restricting to natural-valued rows. Review178.natural_iff_source in /workspace/review/scratch.lean proves this equivalence without using the problem theorem. Positive-integer and one-based-index conversions were also checked.

review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the qualitative problem. The d=0 and m=0 cases are harmless; StrictMono ensures infinite rows; the sign restriction and quantifier scopes are correct. The positive answer and solved category agree with Beck (1981). The linked formal proof has the same conclusion and kernel-checks with only standard axioms after changing one now-redundant `dsimp` to `try dsimp` for the installed Lean/Mathlib version. Direct access to erdosproblems.com was blocked by Cloudflare, so the statement was checked against the original 1979 and 1980 sources. Beck (2017) was accessible only through its abstract; the ancillary docstring attribution of the d^(4+ε) refinement was not independently verified from the full chapter. The reviewed file was not modified.
